Chase refuses to authorize any transaction once a card is reported lost or stolen, and sends a replacement card with a new number; for a credit card the account itself stays open and keeps its age for credit reporting.

Chase monitors cards around the clock and may contact the customer by text message, push notification, email or phone call to confirm whether unusual activity was authorized; fraud alerts are automatic and need no enrollment. Chase can refuse to authorize a transaction it reasonably believes may be fraudulent, but doesn’t say it holds a payment pending the customer's reply.

The law, for the debit card: Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act's Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.6(b), a consumer who reports a lost or stolen debit card within two business days of learning of it owes at most the lesser of $50 or the transfers made before notice; after two business days the cap rises to $500. Transfers shown on a periodic statement that aren't reported within 60 days of the statement being sent carry unlimited liability for transfers after that 60-day window. The 2- and 60-day clocks run from different starts: learning of the loss, and the statement's transmittal.

For the credit card: Truth in Lending Act, Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(b)(1)(ii): a cardholder's liability for unauthorized credit card use is capped at the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained before the card issuer is notified.

A payment reported as not yours: Regulation E, 12 CFR 1005.11: the bank must decide within 10 business days (20 for a new account's first 30 days); if it takes longer it must provisionally credit the account within 10 business days and may take up to 45 days, or 90 days for point-of-sale debit card, out-of-state or new-account transfers. How This Works

You’re enrolled from May 1, 2027. Public cover depends on your income in a month. Medicaid (Medi-Cal in California, HUSKY D in Connecticut) covers you up to 138% of the poverty line. In New York the Essential Plan covers you up to 200%, and in Connecticut Covered Connecticut covers you up to 175% of the previous year’s line. Each is open at any time, with no premium. Covered Connecticut is for an income over HUSKY D’s line, whatever your immigration status, and comes with the premium tax credit from 100% of the poverty line. From 2027 a student in F-1 status or a graduate on OPT gets no premium tax credit. From 2027 Medicaid also has work rules. You meet them in any month you spend some of at the School, or in a month with $580.00 of income (pay, interest, a benefit or a pension). In Connecticut that’s the month before you apply, or any one of the 6 months before a renewal. You also meet them if you’re 65 or over, if you get SNAP under its own work rules, or if you ask for a hospital stay to count. If you don’t meet them, a notice gives you 30 days from when you receive it to answer before an application is denied or cover ends. An ending is announced at least 10 days ahead, at the end of a month. On a marketplace plan you pay the whole premium each month, and your tax return gives back what’s over your share of income, a nonresident’s 1040-NR too. There’s no credit over 400% of the poverty line, since the enhanced credits ended with 2025.
